scenes.title: Previously: tool calling by hand
flow: A joke still read a file

captions.text: Recap of chapter 10: the model replied with JSON that named a tool.
A dict turned that name into a function, and your code ran it.
Errors went back to the model as text.
But the schema forced a tool every time. Even a joke read a file.
Today's black box: the tool calling built into model APIs.
Let's open it.
This is the core of native.py. Here's a question it can answer with one tool.
The model asked for read_file, your code ran it, and the model answered.
Now the joke from chapter 10. Predict: will it read a file?
No tool this time. It went straight to this return.
By hand it asked for a tool 5 times out of 5. Native: 0 out of 5.
This question needs two files. Predict: how many tools will it ask for?
Two, in a single reply. That's why we loop over the calls.
Each result goes back with the role tool.
There's no Friday file. run_tool is chapter 10's dispatch.
The error went back as text, and the model reported it honestly.
So how did the model know the tools? You describe each one in tools.py.
Each definition has a name and says what the tool does.
Its parameters are a JSON schema, like the ones from chapter 08.
Your chat function has two changes.
It sends the tools with every request.
And it returns the whole message, because a tool request isn't in the text.
peek.py is provided. Its first part prints the whole reply.
content is empty. tool_calls is a list, and the arguments are already a dict.

scenes.title: By hand versus native
flow: Tools: in SYSTEM, now in tools=
Result: user message, now role tool
No tool needed: now it just answers

captions.text: Side by side: the tools move from your prompt to the tools field.
You no longer parse the request yourself.
Results get their own role.
And the model can choose not to use a tool.
"Read the Monday sales file." gives no path. Predict: what will the model try?
With the descriptions, it found the path 5 times out of 5.
Without them, it made up a name 5 times out of 5. A tool description is a prompt.

scenes.start: print("3. What the model really writes")

captions.text: But a model can only produce text. So what does it really write?
This skips the chat API and sends the raw prompt, with the tools pasted in.
It's text! Ollama spots these tags and fills in tool_calls.
Native tool calling is what you built in chapter 10.
Now the question from chapter 09. It needs a listing, three files and some addition.
Predict: what will one round trip do?
It listed the folder. Then the model asked for a file, and our code had to stop.
It stopped the same way 10 times out of 10. One round trip isn't enough.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You've finished when you see 5 passed.
Your code can now make one complete tool round trip.
Next, you'll turn that round trip into an agent.
